lines.t: I walked the roads of wind and flame,
Chased hollow crowns and empty fame.
The more I gained, the less I knew,
My heart grew cold, my spirit too.
Then through my pride—a broken reed—
Your mercy called my soul to heed.
I fell before Your wounded feet,
And found my ruin made complete.
O YahuShua, gentle King,
You raised my song when I could not sing.
From dust to breath, from wound to shield,
By Your love, by Your life, I’m healed.
The proud may rise in robe and gold,
Their names may stand, their hearts grow cold.
But You, O Lord, know every tear,
You draw the humble close and near.
You clothed my shame in grace untold,
A beggar wrapped in Heaven’s fold.
Where sin once ruled, Your light revealed—
By Your life, O Lord, I’m healed.
The flower fades, the fields decay,
The gold of men shall fade away.
Yet still Your mercy blooms anew,
Each dawn it paints the world in You.
My heart now rests, my striving ceased,
Your truth my song, Your love my peace.
The grave gives way, the scars are sealed—
By Your life, O Lord, I’m healed.
O YahuShua, Crown of Light,
You turned my darkest wrongs to right.
No longer lost, no longer sealed—
By Your life, O Lord, I’m healed.
